Hi, Roberto. I talked to my director on Tuesday. I'm afraid the news is not great.
Okay. What is his point of view?
He wants to keep the old price. No increase this year.
I see your point, but I'm afraid we can't do that. Our costs went up eight percent this year.
I understand. But he is going to push back on four percent. For us, that is a lot.
That's a fair point. So let's start with the common ground: we both want the June order on time.
Yes, of course. So what can we do?
Maybe we could meet halfway. Two percent now, and two percent in October. It's a compromise, and you have time to plan.
I like that better. But I'm not sure he will say yes without something more.
Then here is an alternative: if you order twenty percent more, the second increase waits until January.
Let's start with the common ground.

In my workshops, I always ask one question. When you disagree with a client, what do you want to keep? Most people say: my price. That is the wrong answer. You want to keep two things: the deal and the relationship. So here is a simple rule. Disagree with the idea, never with the person. Do not say: you are wrong. Say: I see your point, but the numbers say something different. Then look for the common ground. What do both sides want? Start there, and the rest of the conversation is easier. And one more thing. Never push back without an alternative. If you only say no, the other side has nowhere to go. If you say no, and then, maybe we could try this, you are still negotiating. A good no always comes with a next step.

Hi, Roberto, it's Paula. I read your proposal for Lakeshore, the two percent now and two percent in October. I see your point, and I know we need this order. But I'm not sure October works for us. Our new costs start in July, not in October, so for three months we lose money on every box. I'm afraid the finance team is going to push back. Maybe we could do it a little differently. What if the second increase starts in August? It is still a compromise for Megan, and we do not lose three months. It is a small change, but I think it is important. Can we talk before you call her on Monday? I am free after two.
